Main.id: Empower Field at Mile High - Wikipedia#1
Main.sentence: Empower Field at Mile High [note 1] is an ___E:American football U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_football)___ ___E:stadium U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stadium)___ in ___E:Denver U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Denver)___ , Colorado, United States.

Main.id: Empower Field at Mile High - Wikipedia#3

Main.id: Empower Field at Mile High - Wikipedia#4
Main.sentence: The venue was previously home of the ___E:Denver Outlaws U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Denver_Outlaws)___ lacrosse team and the ___E:Colorado Rapids U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Rapids)___ soccer team. Main.id: Empower Field at Mile High - Wikipedia#5
Main.sentence: The stadium is nicknamed "Mile High" due to not only its predecessor, but due to the city's elevation of 1 mile or 5,280 feet (1,610 m) above sea level.

Main.id: Empower Field at Mile High - Wikipedia#6
Main.sentence: Given the difficulty of competing at altitude, as well as the notoriously loud fans, the Broncos are known to have one of the best home-field advantages in the NFL.

Main.sentence: On March 24, 2022, a fire broke out that damaged some suites and many seats on the third level.

Main.id: Empower Field at Mile High - Wikipedia#8

Main.id: Empower Field at Mile High - Wikipedia#9
Main.sentence: The stadium is expected to be replaced by ___E:a new stadium U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Broncos_Stadium)___ in 2031.

Main.id: Empower Field at Mile High - Wikipedia#10
Main.sentence: The Broncos' pursuit of the new stadium included a lobbying effort that included 13 lawyers and tens of thousands of dollars.

Main.id: Empower Field at Mile High - Wikipedia#11
Main.sentence: This effort was directed at the passing of SB 171 which put Referendum 4A on the November 1998 ballot.

Main.id: Empower Field at Mile High - Wikipedia#12
Main.sentence: SB 171 was sponsored by Representative ___E:Doug Dean U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doug_Dean)___ (R) from ___E:Colorado Springs U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Springs)___ .

Main.id: Empower Field at Mile High - Wikipedia#13
Main.sentence: Members of the state legislature claimed that this was one of the largest lobbying efforts they had seen.

Main.id: Empower Field at Mile High - Wikipedia#14
Main.sentence: In November 1998, Denver voters passed referendum 4A which was in favor of the construction of a new football stadium to replace the existing Mile High Stadium.

Main.id: Empower Field at Mile High - Wikipedia#15
Main.sentence: The referendum was included on the ballots of six Colorado counties that comprise the ___E:Denver Metropolitan area U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Denver_metropolitan_area)___ .

Main.id: Empower Field at Mile High - Wikipedia#16
Main.sentence: The referendum called for the extension of a tenth of a percent sales tax on transactions within the Metro area to go towards the cost of issuing a $224.9 million bond.  This tax was originally established in 1990 when the ___E:Colorado Rockies U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Rockies)___ sought public financing for ___E:Coors Field U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coors_Field)___ .

Main.id: Empower Field at Mile High - Wikipedia#17
Main.sentence: Financing and construction for the stadium was monitored by the Metropolitan Football Stadium District (MFSD).

Main.id: Empower Field at Mile High - Wikipedia#18
Main.sentence: The MFSD is a subdivision of the State of Colorado that, "was created for the purpose of planning, acquiring land and constructing a professional football stadium".

Main.id: Empower Field at Mile High - Wikipedia#19
Main.sentence: The MFSD is also responsible for implementing the MFSD tax.  The extension of the original stadium tax came into effect on January 1, 2001.

Main.id: Empower Field at Mile High - Wikipedia#20
Main.sentence: The funding deal between the Broncos and the State of Colorado called for the team to pay 25% of the estimated cost of $400 million while the state would pay the other 75% of the cost. Part of the agreement stipulated that the MFSD would collect half of the ten-year, $120 million naming rights deal with Invesco Funds Group.

Main.id: Empower Field at Mile High - Wikipedia#21
Main.sentence: Upon Sports Authority's bankruptcy, the Broncos agreed to pay the MFSD $3.6 million to assume ownership of the naming rights of the stadium.

Main.id: Empower Field at Mile High - Wikipedia#22
Main.sentence: ___E:Invesco U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Invesco)___ paid $120 million for the original naming rights in 2001, before ___E:Sports Authority U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sports_Authority)___ secured them in August 2011.

Main.id: Empower Field at Mile High - Wikipedia#23
Main.sentence: Despite its sponsor's ___E:liquidation U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liquidation)___ and closure in 2016, the ___E:Sports Authority U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sports_Authority)___ name remained on the stadium for two years afterwards because of regulatory hurdles.

Main.id: Empower Field at Mile High - Wikipedia#24
Main.sentence: The Broncos announced on January 2, 2018, that the stadium's exterior signage would be removed.

Main.id: Empower Field at Mile High - Wikipedia#25

Main.sentence: As part of their offerings, Aramark has partnered with several Denver restaurants to provide a more robust selection of food options.
